L61@P1: Methotrexate can be used at very high doses (> 1 g) in certain neoplastic conditions. Disease states that have been successfully
L62@P1: treated with high-dose methotrexate either alone or in combination with other cytostatics are acute lymphatic leukaemia,
L63@P1: osteogenic sarcoma and certain solid tumours. High-dose therapy is usually given as an infusion over 24 h.
L64@P1: High doses may cause the precipitation of methotrexate or its metabolites in the renal tubules. A high fluid throughput and
L65@P1: alkalisation of the urine to pH 6.5-7.0 by oral or intravenous administration of sodium bicarbonate (e.g., 5 times 625 mg tablets
L66@P1: every three hours) or acetazolamide (e.g., 500 mg orally four times a day) is recommended as a preventive measure.

L164@P3: Impaired hepatic function
L165@P3: Methotrexate should be administered with great caution, if at all, to patients with significant current or previous liver disease,
L166@P3: especially when caused by alcohol. Methotrexate is contraindicated if bilirubin values are >5 mg/dl (85.5 micromole/l) (see
L167@P3: section 4.3).
L168@P3: Patients with pathologic fluid accumulation
L169@P3: Methotrexate elimination is reduced in patients with pathological fluid accumulation (third space fluids) such as ascites or
L170@P3: pleural effusions that may lead to prolonged methotrexate plasma elimination half-life and unexpected toxicity. Pleural
L171@P3: effusions and ascites should be drained prior to initiation of methotrexate treatment. Methotrexate dose should be reduced
L172@P3: according to the serum methotrexate concentrations.
L173@P3: Elderly
L174@P3: Dose reduction should be considered in elderly patients due to reduced liver and kidney function as well as lower folate
L175@P3: reserves which occur with increased age.

L179@P4: 4.3 Contraindications
L180@P4:  Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
L181@P4:  Liver insufficiency (see section 4.2).
L182@P4:  Alcohol abuse.
L183@P4:  Renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance less than 30 ml/min) for methotrexate doses <100 mg/m2, and moderate
L184@P4: renal impairment (creatinine clearance less than 60 ml/min) for methotrexate doses >100 mg/m2 (see section 4.2).
L185@P4:  Pre-existing blood dyscrasias, such as bone marrow hypoplasia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, or significant
L186@P4: anaemia.
L187@P4:  Serious, acute or chronic infections such as tuberculosis and HIV.
L188@P4:  Ulcers of the oral cavity and known active gastrointestinal ulcer disease.
L189@P4:  Pregnancy, breast-feeding (see section 4.6).
L190@P4:  Concurrent vaccination with live vaccines.
L191@P4: 4.4 Special warnings and precautions for use
L192@P4: Patients undergoing therapy should be subject to appropriate supervision so that signs of possible toxic effects or adverse
L193@P4: reactions may be detected and evaluated with minimal delay. Therefore methotrexate should only be administered by, or
L194@P4: under the supervision of physicians whose knowledge and experience includes the use of antimetabolite therapy. Because of
L195@P4: the possibility of severe or even fatal toxic reactions, the patient should be fully informed of the risks involved and the
L196@P4: recommended safety measures.
L197@P4: It should be emphasized to the patient treated for psoriasis that the recommended dose must be used only once a week. The
L198@P4: prescriber should specify the day of intake on the prescription. Patients should be instructed on the importance of adhering to
L199@P4: the once-weekly intakes, and that mistaken daily use of the recommended dose has led to fatal toxicity (see sections 4.2 and
L200@P4: 4.9).
L201@P4: Methotrexate should be used with extreme caution in the presence of debility, in the elderly and in very young children.
L202@P4: Use caution when administering high-dose methotrexate to patients receiving proton pump inhibitor (PPI) therapy (see section
L203@P4: 4.5). Case reports and published population pharmacokinetic studies suggest that concomitant use of some PPIs, such as
L204@P4: omeprazole, esomeprazole and pantoprazole, with methotrexate (primarily at high dose), may elevate and prolong serum
L205@P4: levels of methotrexate and/or its metabolite hydroxymethotrexate, possibly leading to methotrexate toxicities. In two of these
L206@P4: cases, delayed methotrexate elimination was observed when high-dose methotrexate was coadministered with PPIs, but was
L207@P4: not observed when methotrexate was coadministered with ranitidine. However, no formal drug interaction studies of
L208@P4: methotrexate with ranitidine have been conducted.
L209@P4: Cases of severe neurological adverse reactions that ranged from headache to paralysis, coma and stroke-like episodes have
L210@P4: been reported mostly in juveniles and adolescents given methotrexate in combination with cytarabine.
L211@P4: Cases of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) have been reported in patients receiving methotrexate, mostly in
L256@P5: liver cirrhosis developed in isolated cases without any elevation of transaminases.
L257@P5:  Renal function: Methotrexate therapy in patients with impaired renal function should be undertaken with extreme
L258@P5: caution because impairment of renal function will decrease methotrexate elimination.
L259@P5: Renal function should be monitored by renal function tests and urinalyses. If serum creatinine levels are increased, the dose
L260@P5: should be reduced. If creatinine clearance is less than 30 ml/min, treatment with methotrexate should not be given. If
L261@P5: creatinine clearance is less than 60 ml/min, methotrexate doses >100 mg/m2 not be given (see section 4.2 and 4.3).
L262@P5: Treatment with methotrexate doses of >100 mg/m2 should not be initiated at urinary pH values of less than 7.0. Alkalinisation
L263@P5: of the urine must be tested by repeated pH monitoring (value greater than or equal to 6.8) for at least the first 24 hours after
L264@P5: the administration of methotrexate is started.
L265@P5: Methotrexate may cause renal damage that may lead to acute renal failure. Close attention to renal function including
L266@P5-6: adequate hydration, urine alkalinization, and measurement of serum methotrexate and renal function are recommended.Health Products Regulatory Authority

L168@P5: Injection site reactions
L169@P5: The use of central venous access is strongly recommended (see section 4.2). Patients may develop a
L170@P5: potentially severe injection site reaction when trabectedin is administered through a peripheral venous
L171@P5: line.
L172@P5: Trabectedin extravasation may cause tissue necrosis requiring debridement. There is no specific
L173@P5: antidote for extravasation of trabectedin. Extravasation should be managed by local standard practice.
L174@P5: Allergic Reactions
L175@P5: During postmarketing experience, hypersensitivity reactions with very rare occurrence of fatal
L176@P5: outcome, have been reported in association with trabectedin administration either alone or in
L177@P5: combination with PLD (see sections 4.3 and 4.8).
L178@P5: Cardiac Dysfunction
L179@P5: Patients should be monitored for cardiac-related adverse events or myocardial dysfunction.
L180@P5: A thorough cardiac assessment including determination of left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) by
L181@P5: echocardiogram or multigated acquisition scan (MUGA) should be conducted before initiation of
L182@P5: trabectedin and at 2 to 3-month intervals thereafter until trabectedin is discontinued.
L183@P5: Patients with LVEF less than the lower limit of normal (LVEF < LLN), prior cumulative anthracycline
L184@P5: dose of >300mg/m2
L185@P5: , aged > 65 years, or a history of cardiovascular disease (especially in those with
L186@P5: cardiac medication) may be at increased risk of cardiac dysfunction at treatment with trabectedin as
L187@P5: monotherapy or in combination with doxorubicin.
L188@P5: For patients with Grade 3 or 4 cardiac adverse events indicative of cardiomyopathy or for patients with
L189@P5: a LVEF that decreases below the LLN (assessed as either an absolute decrease of LVEF of ≥15% or
L190@P5: <LLN with an absolute decrease of ≥5%), trabectedin should be discontinued.
L191@P5: Capillary Leak Syndrome (CLS)
L192@P5: Cases of Capillary Leak Syndrome (CLS) have been reported with trabectedin (including cases with
L193@P5: fatal outcomes). If symptoms of possible CLS develop, such as unexplained oedema with or without
L194@P5: hypotension, the treating physician should reassess serum albumin level. A rapid decline in serum
L195@P5: albumin level may be indicative of CLS. If a diagnosis of CLS is confirmed after exclusion of other
L196@P5: causes, the treating physician should discontinue trabectedin and initiate CLS treatment according to
L197@P5-6: institutional guidelines (see sections 4.2 and 4.8).7
L198@P6: Others
L199@P6: Co-administration of Yondelis with potent inhibitors of the enzyme CYP3A4 should be avoided (see
L200@P6: section 4.5). If this is not possible, close monitoring of toxicities are required and dose reductions of
L201@P6: trabectedin should be considered.
L202@P6: Caution should be taken if medicinal products associated with hepatotoxicity are administered
L203@P6: concomitantly with trabectedin, since the risk of hepatotoxicity may be increased.
L204@P6: Concomitant use of trabectedin with phenytoin may reduce phenytoin absorption leading to an
L205@P6: exacerbation of convulsions. Combination of trabectedin with phenytoin or live attenuated vaccines is
L206@P6: not recommended and with yellow fever vaccine is specifically contraindicated (see section 4.3).
L207@P6: The concomitant use of trabectedin with alcohol must be avoided (see section 4.5).
L208@P6: Women of childbearing potential must use highly effective contraception during treatment and 8
L209@P6: months thereafter, and immediately inform the treating physician if a pregnancy occurs (see section
L210@P6: 5.3).
L211@P6: Men in fertile age must use highly effective contraception during treatment and 5 months after
L212@P6: treatment (see section 4.6).
L213@P6: This medicine contains potassium, less than 1 mmol (39 mg) per vial, i.e. essentially “potassium-free”.
L214@P6: See also PLD Summary of Product Characteristics for more detailed information on warnings and
L215@P6: precautions.

L436@P10: hepatic injury were uncommon with a lower than 1% incidence of individual signs and symptoms

L439@P10: Other adverse reactions
L440@P10: Hepatic failure: Rare cases of hepatic failure (including cases with fatal outcomes) have been reported
L441@P10: in patients with serious underlying medical conditions treated with trabectedin, both in clinical trials
L442@P10: and in post marketing setting. Some potential risk factors that may have contributed to increased
L443@P10: trabectedin toxicity observed in these cases were dose management inconsistent with recommended
L444@P10: guidelines, potential CYP3A4 interaction due to multiple competing CYP3A4 substrates or CYP3A4
L445@P10: inhibitors, or lack of dexamethasone prophylaxis.
L446@P10: Capillary Leak Syndrome (CLS): Cases of Capillary Leak Syndrome (CLS) have been reported with
L447@P10: trabectedin (including cases with fatal outcomes) (see section 4.4).
L448@P10: Reporting of suspected adverse reactions
L449@P10: Reporting suspected adverse reactions after authorisation of the medicinal product is important. It
L450@P10: allows continued monitoring of the benefit/risk balance of the medicinal product. Healthcare
L451@P10: professionals are asked to report any suspected adverse reactions via the national reporting system
L452@P10: listed in Appendix V.
L453@P10: 4.9 Overdose
L454@P10: There is limited data on the effects of trabectedin overdose. The major anticipated toxicities are
L455@P10: gastrointestinal, bone marrow suppression and hepatic toxicity. There is no specific antidote for
L456@P10: trabectedin currently available. In the event of an overdose, patients should be closely monitored and
L457@P10: symptomatic supportive care measures instituted as required.
L458@P10: 5. PHARMACOLOGICAL PROPERTIES
L459@P10: 5.1 Pharmacodynamic properties
L460@P10: Pharmacotherapeutic group: Antineoplastic agent, ATC code: L01CX01.
L461@P10: Mechanism of action
L462@P10: Trabectedin binds to the minor groove of deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), bending the helix to the major
L463@P10: groove. This binding to DNA triggers a cascade of events affecting several transcription factors, DNA
L464@P10-11: binding proteins, and DNA repair pathways, resulting in perturbation of the cell cycle. 12
L465@P11: Pharmacodynamic effects
L466@P11: Trabectedin has been shown to exert antiproliferative in vitro and in vivo activity against a range of
L467@P11: human tumour cell lines and experimental tumours, including malignancies such as sarcoma, breast,
L468@P11: non-small cell lung, ovarian and melanoma.
L469@P11: Electrocardiogram (ECG) investigations
L470@P11: In a placebo-controlled QT/QTc study, trabectedin did not prolong the QTc interval in patients with
L471@P11: advanced solid malignancies.
